title: Crestline Business Points Program Terms — Earning
content:
These terms govern how company points (Crestline Business points) and agreement-year spend are earned under Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements.

### E1. Segments that earn

A flown Crestline segment earns business points when all of the following hold:

- its ticket carries the agreement as the ticket's corporate account;
- when the tier requires the tour code, the ticket carried the agreement's tour code at booking;
- the passenger was on the agreement's active roster on the flight date.

Partner-operated flights earn nothing on a tier where partner-operated flights do not earn business points.

### E2. Points per segment

The clause "Points are the segment's eligible spend times the points per dollar of the tier held on the flight date, rounded down to the whole point" is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis for the points posted on a segment. The definition of eligible spend in E3 remains in force.

### E3. Eligible spend

Eligible spend is the segment's share of the base fare after the negotiated discount, excluding taxes. The same spend is added to the agreement year's qualifying spend.

### E4. Summit miles

The traveler also earns personal Summit miles on the same flight on a tier where the traveler earns Summit miles as well as the company's points.

### E5. Open agreements only

Points accrue — and spend and bonuses post — only while the agreement is active or under review. Segments flown while the agreement is suspended earn nothing and are never credited later. The agreement's status is read from its agreement record.

### E6. Once per segment

A segment already credited is never credited again: a ticket and segment that already carry a points accrual entry on the agreement's points activity receive no second one.

### E7. Claims for tickets booked without the agreement

Points for an eligible ticket booked without the agreement may be claimed within the tier's retroactive claim window, counted in calendar days after the flight date. The clock starts on the flight date shown on the ticket's flown-coupon record for that ticket and segment; the claim date must be not later than the last day of the window, and a claim on that last day is within the window.

| Claim made on | Within the window? |
|---|---|
| the flight date or any calendar day after it up to the last day of the window | yes |
| the last calendar day of the window | yes (the boundary day counts) |
| the calendar day after the last day of the window | no |

Hypothetical dates: with a window of 30 calendar days and a flight dated 10 March, the last day of the window is 9 April; a claim on 9 April is within the window and a claim on 10 April is not.

### E8. Enrollment bonus

The clause "The enrollment bonus of the tier's enrollment-bonus points is credited once when the agreement's flown spend since approval first reaches the tier's enrollment-bonus spend" is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis for the enrollment bonus.

### E9. Spend-milestone bonus

The clause "the milestone bonus of the tier's spend-milestone bonus points is credited once per agreement year when the agreement year's spend first reaches the spend milestone of the tier then held" is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis for the spend-milestone bonus.

superseded_clauses: Points are the segment's eligible spend times points_per_dollar of the tier held on the flight date, rounded down to the whole point
The enrollment bonus of enrollment_bonus_points is credited once when the agreement's flown spend since approval first reaches enrollment_bonus_min_flown_spend_usd
